desc:
An AI agent maintenance starter sprint checks that your agent still works after your tools, prices and rules have changed. Ecom Swift LLC reviews the agent, fixes what has drifted, retests it on your cases and hands you a short written report.

## Why agents need upkeep after launch

An agent is not finished the day it goes live. It sits between a language model, your tools and your business rules, and all three keep moving. A form gains a new field, a spreadsheet column is renamed, a price list changes, or a connected app updates its login method. The agent keeps running, but it starts to give worse answers or fails quietly.

Quiet failure is the real risk. A crashed agent is obvious. An agent that still replies but quotes an old return policy can do harm for weeks before anyone notices.

## What does AI agent maintenance involve?

Agent maintenance is a regular check of the parts that can go stale. It covers the connections to your tools, the prompts and rules that guide the agent, the model it calls, and the results it produces on real cases.

This service is a fixed starter sprint, not a monthly plan. We do one round of review and repair, give you the findings, and you decide whether you want ongoing care. Monthly support, if you want it, is quoted separately.

## What tends to break in an agent

Most problems come from change outside the agent. Common causes include expired or revoked connections, renamed fields, new product lines the agent does not know about, policies written into a prompt that are now out of date, and a model update that shifts the tone or format of replies. Rising usage can also push an agent into limits it never hit before.

Fixing these early is cheaper than fixing them after a customer complains. A short sprint often finds several small faults that together explain why the agent feels less reliable than it did at launch.

## What a good maintenance round covers

- A review of the agent's current instructions against how your business works today.
- A test of every tool connection, including permissions and expired access.
- A look through recent failed or flagged runs to find repeating causes.
- An update of rules, prompts and reference data that have changed.
- A check of which model and tool versions the agent depends on.
- A retest on a set of your own cases, compared with how the agent behaved before.
- A review of limits and approvals, to confirm they still match the risk.
- Updated notes so your team knows how the agent now behaves.
- A short report listing what was fixed, what remains and what to watch.

## How we work

We begin by reading the agent's setup and its recent run history. Then we test each connection one by one, since a single dead link can explain many odd results. We list the faults in order of impact and agree with you what to fix inside the sprint.

After the fixes, we run your cases again and compare the output with the earlier results, so you can see whether the agent improved. The report ends with a short list of things worth checking next quarter. The Basic package is a health check with a fix list. The Standard package adds repairs and updated rules for one agent. The Premium package covers several agents and a deeper review of models and tools.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Tell us what changed in your business since the agent launched.
- Keep a list of your test cases and add new ones when you meet an odd result.
- Review the agent after any change to prices, policies or connected tools.
- Keep the agent's instructions in one place that more than one person can read.
- Schedule a light check at regular intervals.

**Avoid:**
- Assuming silence means the agent is working properly.
- Editing prompts directly in production without a retest.
- Letting several people change rules without a record.
- Ignoring failed runs because the next run succeeded.
- Treating one successful demo as proof the agent is healthy.

## Who this is for

This service suits an owner whose agent worked well at launch but now makes mistakes. It suits a team that has changed its CRM, help desk or price list and wants to be sure the agent kept up. It also suits anyone who inherited an agent from a freelancer and wants an independent check, including agents we did not build.

## What we need from you

Send us access to the agent and its connected tools as a collaborator, team member or developer user, wherever the platform supports it, plus a short note on what has changed. Share a few cases where the agent got it wrong. We never need your passwords, and all fixes are made inside your own accounts.
